title: India in Final-Stage Talks on Expanded BrahMos Missile Sale to Philippines
excerpt: Manila is expected to buy about five BrahMos systems — nearly 60 missiles worth $700 million to $800 million, sources told Reuters — roughly double its $375 million order from 2022.
body:
• India is in final-stage talks to expand its BrahMos missile sale to the Philippines, three sources with direct knowledge of the matter told Reuters; no contract has been announced.
  • The Philippines is expected to buy about five BrahMos systems — nearly 60 missiles — in a deal potentially worth $700 million to $800 million, according to two of the Indian sources.
  • The likely deal is roughly double the $375 million BrahMos order the Philippines placed in 2022 for naval use, deliveries under which are nearing completion.
  • Philippine Defence Secretary Gilberto Teodoro said at the Delhi Defence Dialogue on Wednesday that Manila hopes to secure more BrahMos units and has shared a wish list with India; India's defence and foreign ministries and BrahMos Aerospace did not respond to Reuters' requests for comment.

India is in final-stage talks to sell more BrahMos supersonic cruise missiles to the Philippines, three sources with direct knowledge of the matter told Reuters, as New Delhi nears completion of deliveries under the two countries' 2022 deal. The talks have not produced an announced contract, and the size and value of the expected deal are reported figures from the sources, not confirmed terms.

What is being discussed

The Philippines is expected to buy about five BrahMos systems, nearly 60 missiles in total, in a deal potentially worth $700 million to $800 million, two of the Indian sources said. Reuters is the first to report the size and value of the expected deal.

"Manila has shown interest again to procure about 5 systems of the BrahMos and they now view India as a very reliable partner."

— Indian source, speaking to Reuters

The expected package is much larger than the Philippines' last BrahMos order — $375 million for naval use under the 2022 deal. BrahMos, developed jointly by India and Russia, is among the world's fastest cruise missiles and can be launched from land, sea and air platforms.

What Manila has said publicly

The Philippine side has confirmed the interest, if not the numbers. Arsenio Andolong, a Philippines defence ministry spokesperson, told Reuters that President Ferdinand Marcos Jr had expressed his desire to acquire additional BrahMos missiles, without offering more details.

Speaking virtually at the Delhi Defence Dialogue on Wednesday, Philippine Defence Secretary Gilberto Teodoro said the Philippines hoped to secure more BrahMos units and had shared a wish list with Indian authorities to make the system more tailored to the Philippine environment. India's defence and foreign ministries, and the missile maker BrahMos Aerospace, did not respond to requests for comment.

Why the Philippines wants more

Manila is modernising its military and strengthening its coastal defences as tensions rise in the disputed South China Sea, where the Philippines and China have clashed in recent years over overlapping claims. Additional shore-based BrahMos systems would extend the reach of that coastal defence — which is why this is an expansion of an existing deployment rather than a new capability for the Philippines.

What it means for India's defence exports

Interest in BrahMos has increased since last year's four-day conflict between India and Pakistan, when India used the system in battle for the first time, according to Reuters. In July, Delhi announced the supply of BrahMos missiles to Indonesia and has also signed a deal with Vietnam; it is in talks on the system with a number of other countries, including the UAE, Thailand, South Africa and Brazil.

The wider numbers show why a second Philippine order matters to New Delhi. India's defence exports for the fiscal year to March reached 384.24 billion rupees ($4.11 billion), a jump of more than 62% from the same period the year before, government data showed. A $700 million to $800 million Philippine deal, if signed, would be one of the largest single orders behind that growth. The next step to watch is a signed contract: final-stage talks, as reported, are not yet a deal.
image_caption: A BrahMos missile system passes along Rajpath in New Delhi during a Republic Day parade rehearsal. India is in final-stage talks to sell the Philippines about five more BrahMos systems, according to Reuters.
nri_angle: A second, larger Philippine BrahMos order would mark India's emergence as a missile exporter of consequence, a shift in the country's strategic weight that diaspora readers track closely.
